label: New York x Workers' Compensation
source: Assembled without Ahrefs, which had no API units left until 2026-09-19. Candidates came from Google Places text search across New York City and its five boroughs (scripts/discover_places.py, 185 domains), and each was kept only where the firm's own site publishes a workers' compensation practice page: named in the address, titled for the practice, and carrying something specific to it rather than a passing mention (scripts/check_practice.py). Blog posts, glossaries and question pages do not count. The four Ahrefs metrics are unmeasured, so D2 scores pending for every firm here until the subscription resets.

unresolved_notes.samndan.com: Meirowitz & Wasserberg appeared in five of the six searches but publishes no workers' compensation practice page we could find, so it is out of the cohort rather than ranked in a practice it does not hold itself out for.
unresolved_notes.rmfwlaw.com: Rosenberg, Minc, Falkoff & Wolff publishes workers' compensation only as blog posts under /blog/. Writing about the practice is not holding yourself out for it.
unresolved_notes.msainjurylaw.com: Marc S. Albert's only compensation page is an answer to a question, which is the same content-marketing page with a friendlier address.
unresolved_notes.855dolor55.com: The Ward Law Group's only compensation page is 'Workers Comp vs Personal Injury', a comparison piece whose address gives no sign of it. The title did.
unresolved_notes.brandonjbroderick.com: Held back from publication on 2026-09-13. The state's attorney register records one of the twenty-five attorneys this firm names as suspended, and the registration itself names the firm, so the match is not a namesake. A suspension in New York is imposed by the Appellate Division, including for failure to register, and the register does not say which this is. Publishing a twenty-five-attorney firm as Not eligible, and a named lawyer as disciplined, on a status whose cause we have not read, is not a claim this evidence supports. It needs a person to read the underlying order.
